title: Idempotency: stable handoff key + optional client idempotency token on keyless writes

epic.name: Coordination Bus v2 (re-scoped): Repo Coordination Bus

story.as_a: coding agent (or the /handoff skill) whose write may double-fire on retry or offline reconcile
story.i_want_to: post a handoff under a stable, deterministic key so a duplicate dedups instead of creating a second pointer
story.so_that: a retried /handoff does not pile up duplicate pointers, and even when a cross-session re-fire does leave a second pointer the WORK is still handled exactly once (deduped at the claim layer)

rationale: The panel's agreed-gap #5: keyless posts are append-only, so a retried/offline-reconciled write duplicates the row — there is no client idempotency token, unlike knowledge_create (which has idempotency_key, knowledge.ex:240, 302-311). SCOPE (corrected): the stable-key upsert dedups only a SAME-SESSION re-fire (the slot key includes session_id + the server-stamped agent_id, channel_post.ex/coordination.ex), so a re-fire from a DIFFERENT session — the exact offline-reconcile case — writes a NEW slot row. Three layers cover the cases: (1) a handoff carries a STABLE key `handoff:<anchor>` so a same-session retry upserts one row; (2) an OPTIONAL client idempotency token on the KEYLESS write path dedups a cross-session keyless re-fire, parity with knowledge_create; (3) for a CROSS-SESSION KEYED handoff re-fire, a duplicate POINTER is tolerated (harmless noise, both point at the same durable home) and the WORK is deduped exactly-once at the CLAIM layer (40.B1, keyed on ref, claimant-independent) — B2 does NOT promise cross-session keyed pointer dedup.

background.reference: panel agreed-gap #5 ('No idempotency') and 'The /handoff skill posting a KEYLESS message -- TROUBLE ... must carry a stable key'; knowledge_create's idempotency_key (knowledge.ex:240, 268, 278-311, get_article_by_idempotency_key/3 :621-635); the existing keyed-slot upsert (insert_opts/1, coordination.ex).
background.includes: A stable-key convention for handoffs + an optional idempotency token column/logic for keyless posts; interacts with the claim layer (40.B1) as the ultimate exactly-once backstop.

acceptance_criteria.description: A handoff post carries a stable `key` of the form `handoff:<anchor>` (deterministic from the handoff's durable-home anchor, e.g. `handoff:repo#812`). Because a keyed post upserts the caller's own per-session slot (insert_opts/1, coordination.ex, whose uniqueness includes session_id + the server-stamped agent_id), a SAME-SESSION re-fire refreshes the SAME row (no duplicate). SCOPE — this dedups the same-session retry ONLY: a re-fire from a DIFFERENT session (the offline-reconcile case) has a different session_id and creates a SEPARATE pointer row; that duplicate pointer is TOLERATED (harmless noise). Documented: the stable key makes a same-session /handoff retry-safe; the CLAIM (40.B1, keyed on ref, claimant-independent) — NOT the pointer — is the cross-session exactly-once backstop for the WORK. B2.1 does not claim to prevent cross-session duplicate pointers.

An OPTIONAL client idempotency token is accepted on the KEYLESS write path: when supplied, a repeat write with the same (tenant_id, project_id, agent_id, idempotency_key) returns the EXISTING post ({created: false}) instead of appending a duplicate — the same guarantee as knowledge_create (knowledge.ex:302-311). Implemented via an `idempotency_key` column + a partial unique index `WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL`, caught with unique_constraint and resolved to the existing row (get-by-idempotency pattern, knowledge.ex:621-635).

The idempotency token is bounded, blank-normalized to nil, and NUL/secret-scanned like other text fields (channel_post.ex:57, 129); absent, the write is exactly today's append-only behavior (US-39.2). The token is scoped to (tenant, project, agent) so one agent's token never collides with another's.

The write endpoint + MCP channel_post tool accept an optional `idempotency_key`; the response distinguishes created vs deduped (reuse the created/updated signal, run_post/3 coordination.ex:313-341 / post_outcome/1 :371-372, or an explicit {:ok, post, :deduplicated}). The MCP tool documents that a handoff should pass a stable key and (for keyless reconcile) an idempotency token.

test_cases.name: same-session handoff re-fire upserts one slot
steps: the same session posts key=handoff:repo#812 again (retry)
expected_results: one row (upserted, 200), not two; body/refs refreshed

test_cases.name: keyless write with idempotency token dedups
expected_results: first: 201 created; second: returns the SAME post id, created:false, no duplicate row

test_cases.name: different agents, same token, no collision
preconditions: agent A and agent B in the same tenant/project
steps: A posts idempotency_key=abc; B posts idempotency_key=abc
expected_results: two distinct posts (token is scoped per-agent); neither dedups the other

test_cases.name: no token = append-only (unchanged)
steps: POST twice with same body, no key, no token

test_cases.name: double-fired handoff does not double-claim
steps: fire /handoff twice for repo#812 (stable key + a claim on ref handoff:repo#812)
expected_results: one pointer post + at most one open claim; the second claim is 409 already_claimed

technical_notes: Stable-key path needs NO schema change — it reuses the shipped keyed-slot upsert (insert_opts/1, coordination.ex). The convention `handoff:<anchor>` is enforced client-side (the /handoff skill, a claude-config companion) but MUST be documented server-side so the read/discovery treats it consistently.

Idempotency token: migration adds `idempotency_key text NULL` + `create unique_index(:channel_posts, [:tenant_id, :project_id, :agent_id, :idempotency_key], where: "idempotency_key IS NOT NULL", name: :channel_posts_idempotency_uidx)`. Mirror the knowledge_create dedup exactly (knowledge.ex:302-311, get_article_by_idempotency_key/3 :621-635): on unique-violation, SELECT the existing row and return it as deduped.

Schema: field :idempotency_key, :string; add to cast (channel_post.ex:128), normalize_blank (:129), @scanned_text_fields (:57), a bounded validate_length. NEVER part of the working-state slot key (it is a separate dedup dimension).

run_post/3 (coordination.ex:313-341): on the keyless path with a token, either try-insert-and-recover-on-conflict, or pre-check via a get-by-idempotency helper then insert — prefer the insert-and-recover (no TOCTOU), matching the claim pattern (40.B1) and knowledge_create.

40.B1 (claim) is the true cross-session exactly-once mechanism; B2 dedups the POINTER write only within a session (stable key) or on the keyless path (idempotency token). A cross-session KEYED handoff re-fire still leaves a duplicate pointer — tolerated noise — and the WORK is deduped exactly-once by B1's claim (keyed on ref, claimant-independent). So: B2 reduces duplicate pointers where it cheaply can; B1 guarantees exactly-once WORK. If cross-session keyed pointer dedup is ever wanted, allow the optional idempotency token on the keyed path too (out of scope here).
MCP: add optional idempotency_key to channel_post (mcp-server/index.js ~440, ~2266-2296) and document the handoff stable-key convention.
